links.outcome: Readability of genAI outputs (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) versus clinical leaflets
links.effect: genAI outputs required 2–3 more years of education to understand than leaflets.
links.quote: Moreover, genAI outputs required 2–3 more years of education to understand.

links.outcome: Inclusion of safety-netting in genAI eye health advice
links.effect: Both models failed to include appropriate safety-netting; safety scores otherwise comparable across sources.
links.quote: Safety scores were comparable across sources, but both models underreported treatment complications, exhibited guideline inconsistencies, and failed to include appropriate safety-netting.

links.outcome: Factual alignment, omissions, and guideline consistency of genAI eye advice versus leaflets
links.effect: Higher factual alignment (GPT-5 37.4%, Gemini 3 36.2%, leaflets 30.7%) and fewer omissions (6.7, 7.0 vs 7.9), but guideline inconsistencies and underreported complications.
links.quote: Both genAI models showed higher factual alignment than clinical leaflets (GPT-5 = 37.4%, Gemini 3 = 36.2%, leaflets = 30.7%; both p < 0.001) and fewer omissions (GPT-5 = 6.7, Gemini 3 = 7.0, leaflets = 7.9; both p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks the factual accuracy, safety, comprehensiveness, and readability of generative AI chatbots against clinical patient leaflets for eye health questions without evaluating an implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
